path: MJ Lenderman to Neil Young: the Crazy Horse line
intro: Trunk line 1, Neil Young & Crazy Horse guitar. This route follows Lenderman's loose, loud, long-soloing guitar back through the Molina circle, 2000s Wilco and the SST underground to the band that invented the sound.

steps.connection: Manning Fireworks is the payoff of the Crazy Horse-toned, deadpan songwriting Lenderman worked out two years earlier on Boat Songs.
Boat Songs' ragged, feedback-edged guitar solos resemble the heavy, Crazy Horse-indebted folk rock Arbouretum made in Baltimore a decade before.
The Gathering's long, heavy guitar passages sit close to Wilco's mid-2000s turn toward extended, Crazy Horse-style guitar playing.
A Ghost Is Born's guitar workouts arrived a year after Jason Molina made his own openly Crazy Horse-indebted record.
The Magnolia Electric Co. sounds deeply indebted to Neil Young and Crazy Horse's ragged guitar rock, most directly to the barn-recorded roar of Ragged Glory.
Ragged Glory's roar came after Dinosaur Jr. had spent the late '80s fusing Crazy Horse-scale guitar with hardcore volume, and it seems to have emboldened that whole noisy-guitar underground.
You're Living All Over Me took the distorted Crazy Horse side of Rust Never Sleeps, the record punks cited as proof Young never went soft, and ran it through hardcore.
Rust Never Sleeps' electric side is played by the same Young/Talbot/Molina/Sampedro Crazy Horse lineup that locked into place on Zuma.
Zuma came out the same year as Tonight's the Night, the bleak, earlier-recorded album made with Crazy Horse's rhythm section.
Tonight's the Night was made in mourning for Crazy Horse guitarist Danny Whitten, who fronted the band's own debut album four years earlier.
Crazy Horse's debut gives the band an identity of its own, but its sound was first set on Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere, Young's first album with them.
Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere followed Young's exit from Buffalo Springfield, where 'Broken Arrow' had already hinted at his long-form ambitions.
Buffalo Springfield Again is the top of this line: the band where Neil Young started, before Crazy Horse.

path: Wednesday to the Allman Brothers: the Southern storytelling line
intro: Trunk line 4, Southern storytelling rock. Wednesday's lineage runs through Drive-By Truckers to Lynyrd Skynyrd, the Allmans and the Band. The noise side of the band's sound is traced in the Lenderman and Brown Horse paths.

steps.connection: Rat Saw God fuses Skynyrd-to-Drive-By-Truckers storytelling with Sonic Youth-style guitar noise, and the band's covers set from the year before puts its influences in plain sight.
Mowing the Leaves Instead of Piling 'em Up filters country, indie and classic-rock covers through the same blown-out, pedal-steel sound Wednesday first recorded in full on Twin Plagues.
Twin Plagues grafts noise textures onto Southern storytelling in the Skynyrd-to-Drive-By Truckers line, and that line's modern model is Decoration Day.
Decoration Day builds on the harmonized three-guitar sound the Truckers established on Southern Rock Opera.
Southern Rock Opera is built explicitly on Lynyrd Skynyrd's story, and its climax is the 1977 plane crash that followed the release of Street Survivors.
Street Survivors closes the original Skynyrd lineup's catalog in the same mid-'70s South where Gary Stewart was making honky-tonk sound like rock.
Out of Hand's raw, rock-inflected honky-tonk resembles the country-leaning side of Skynyrd heard on Second Helping.
Second Helping follows directly from the band's debut, which established the Jacksonville three-guitar sound.
Skynyrd's debut sounds indebted to the extended, dual-lead-guitar approach of the Allman Brothers' At Fillmore East.
At Fillmore East stretches out the blues-and-jazz guitar interplay first set down on the Allmans' 1969 debut.
The Allmans' debut arrived the same year as the Band's second album, whose novelistic Southern storytelling the Allmans and, decades later, the Drive-By Truckers sound indebted to.
The Band sits at the top of the Southern storytelling line, the root of the character songs Wednesday tells today.

path: villagerrr to the Velvet Underground: the home-taping line
intro: Trunk line 6, the DIY network. villagerrr's self-released Bandcamp run belongs to a long tradition of homemade records, and this path follows it back through Ohio four-tracks and boombox tapes to the Velvets.

steps.connection: Tear Your Heart Out brought villagerrr's homemade Ohio songwriting to a wider audience, a step up from the 2022 run of self-released uploads that includes OHIOAN.
OHIOAN's regional focus comes from the same quick 2022 run of self-released albums as Like Leaves.
Like Leaves' quiet, homemade Midwestern folk resembles the hushed early records of another Ohio-born songwriter, Jason Molina.
Didn't It Rain came out the same year as the Mountain Goats' All Hail West Texas, the other great early-2000s record of plain songs, barely dressed.
All Hail West Texas is John Darnielle's full-album return to boombox recording, the same home-taping method Elliott Smith used on four-track in the mid-'90s.
Elliott Smith's four-track method descends from the basement-tape aesthetic that Guided by Voices, from Dayton, Ohio, legitimized with Bee Thousand.
Bee Thousand made four-track home recording an aesthetic, alongside Sebadoh, the band Lou Barlow built from his home tapes.
Sebadoh III's four-track ethos sounds deeply indebted to Daniel Johnston's cassettes, handed out around Austin a decade earlier.
Hi, How Are You's plain, childlike directness resembles Jonathan Richman's songs with the Modern Lovers.
Richman was an avowed Velvet Underground devotee, and John Cale produced some of the Modern Lovers sessions.
The Velvet Underground's quiet third album is the top of this line: guitar-based intimacy that home-tapers and slowcore bands have chased ever since.

path: Big Thief to Woody Guthrie: the folk songwriting line
intro: Trunk line 8, folk songwriting. The path follows Big Thief's hushed, plainspoken songs back through Gillian Welch and Townes Van Zandt to Dylan, the Anthology and Guthrie.

steps.connection: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You shares its songwriter, Adrianne Lenker, with the cabin-recorded solo album songs.
songs strips Lenker's writing to voice and guitar, the same quiet mode heard on Big Thief's atmospheric U.F.O.F.
U.F.O.F. pulls the band's folk songwriting toward atmosphere and space, opening out the confessional songs of Capacity.
Capacity deepens the songwriting first heard on the band's debut, Masterpiece.
Masterpiece sounds indebted to the folk-songwriting line that runs through Gillian Welch.
Time (The Revelator)'s long, patient songs grow from the stark duo arrangements of Hell Among the Yearlings.
Hell Among the Yearlings continues directly from Revival's Stanley Brothers and Carter Family influence.
Revival's hushed duo template sits in the folk lineage that runs from the Carter Family through Townes Van Zandt.
Our Mother the Mountain came out of the late-'60s Houston folk clubs, part of the folk revival Dylan's Freewheelin' had turned toward songwriting.
Freewheelin' established Dylan as a songwriter, drawing on the songbook the Anthology of American Folk Music had made available.
The Anthology gathered the Carter Family and their generation, whose melodies Woody Guthrie borrowed.
Dust Bowl Ballads is the top of the folk-songwriting line; Dylan modeled his early persona on Guthrie.

path: Greg Freeman to Blonde on Blonde: country played by punk kids
intro: Trunk line 2, country played by punk and indie kids. From Burlington's indie-country scene, the path runs through Bloodshot Records and the No Depression bands to '80s cowpunk and the Dylan record the Scorchers covered.

steps.connection: Burnover builds on Freeman's place in the Burlington scene alongside Lily Seabird.
Alas comes out of the same Burlington indie-folk-and-rock scene whose twang Florry's Philadelphia records sound of a piece with.
The Holey Bible's caustic Dear Life Records twang sounds close to Greg Freeman's cult breakthrough, I Looked Out.
I Looked Out's loud, ragged indie-twang resembles the Bloodshot Records cowpunk of Lydia Loveless.
Indestructible Machine places Loveless in the Bloodshot lineage that runs back through Whiskeytown and the Old 97's.
Strangers Almanac comes out of the same mid-'90s insurgent-country wave as the Old 97's.
Wreck Your Life made the Old 97's the flagship Texas band on Bloodshot, a roster that sounds indebted to Uncle Tupelo.
Anodyne is the culmination of the arc Uncle Tupelo began on No Depression.
No Depression splices Hüsker Dü-style volume onto Carter Family country.
New Day Rising came out the same year as Tim by the Replacements, Hüsker Dü's Minneapolis peers.
Tim's college-radio punk shared 1985 with the Knitters, the side project in which members of X and the Blasters played straight country.
Poor Little Critter on the Road is the clearest statement of punk kids playing country, alongside Nashville's Jason & the Scorchers, whose Fervor brought cowpunk to a national audience.
Fervor includes the Scorchers' cover of Bob Dylan's 'Absolutely Sweet Marie,' from Blonde on Blonde.
Blonde on Blonde, cut largely with Nashville session players, is the top of this line: a rock songwriter taking his songs to country's capital.

path: Waxahatchee to Kitty Wells: the women's-eye country line
intro: Trunk lines 2 and 8, country by punk and indie kids plus folk songwriting. Katie Crutchfield came up in DIY punk; this path follows her country turn back through Lucinda Williams and Emmylou's Trio to Dolly, Loretta, Patsy and Kitty Wells.

steps.connection: Tigers Blood, with MJ Lenderman on guitar, continues the country-facing sound Crutchfield developed with Jess Williamson in Plains.
I Walked with You a Ways is a direct offshoot of the country pivot Crutchfield made on Saint Cloud.
Saint Cloud's Southern country songwriting has often been compared to Lucinda Williams's Car Wheels on a Gravel Road.
Car Wheels on a Gravel Road is the culmination of songwriting Williams had been building since the early '90s, when Iris DeMent was writing in a similarly plainspoken vein.
Infamous Angel's plain, Ozark-rooted songwriting is close kin to Lucinda Williams's breakthrough self-titled album.
Lucinda Williams arrived a year after Trio, which brought Dolly Parton's Appalachian hard country into Emmylou Harris's circle.
Trio's Dolly Parton had made her own songwriting the center of her records with Coat of Many Colors.
Coat of Many Colors came out the same year as Loretta Lynn's autobiographical Coal Miner's Daughter.
Coal Miner's Daughter extends the blunt first-person voice Lynn introduced on Don't Come Home A-Drinkin'.
Don't Come Home A-Drinkin' came from a singer who counted Patsy Cline as a friend and early champion.
Showcase's torch-style vocals followed the path Kitty Wells had cleared for women singing frankly in country.
Kitty Wells' Country Hit Parade is the top of this line: the plainspoken woman's-eye view in country music.

path: Ryan Davis & the Roadhouse Band to John Prine: the deadpan line
intro: Trunk line 3, deadpan, funny-sad songwriting. The path runs from Davis's Louisville bar-band epics through State Champion, David Berman and the Drag City school to Prine and Tom T. Hall.

steps.connection: New Threats from the Soul continues the long-form storytelling Davis launched with the Roadhouse Band on Dancing on the Edge.
Dancing on the Edge sounds indebted to David Berman, whose last album came out as Purple Mountains.
Purple Mountains came out a year after Send Flowers, Davis's last record with State Champion, which was working the same Berman line.
Send Flowers is a direct predecessor to the Roadhouse Band, grown from State Champion's earlier Fantasy Error.
Fantasy Error sounds indebted to the Drag City lineage that runs to Silver Jews' Nashville-era Tanglewood Numbers.
Tanglewood Numbers continues the Silver Jews' full-band Nashville sound that grew out of the wry, novelistic writing of American Water.
American Water came out on Drag City, the Chicago label that also released Will Oldham's Palace records.
Viva Last Blues is the fullest band record by Louisville's Palace, Drag City labelmates of the early Silver Jews.
Starlite Walker sounds indebted to Prine- and Dylan-style talking-blues songwriting.
Sweet Revenge pulls Prine's storytelling toward honky-tonk, and his closest narrative peer in that world is Tom T. Hall.
The Storyteller's plain first-person narratives make Hall a direct peer of Prine's debut.
John Prine is the top of the deadpan line: the funny-sad storytelling that runs through Drag City to Davis.

path: Brown Horse to the Velvet Underground: Molina and the slow, sad, noisy line
intro: Trunk line 5, slow, sad and noisy textures, reached through the Molina circle. Brown Horse's lineage points at Jason Molina; from his quietest records the path drops into '90s slowcore and back to the Velvets.

steps.connection: All the Right Weaknesses sounds indebted to Jason Molina, as did the band's debut, Reservoir.
Reservoir's Crazy Horse-steeped alt-country resembles Magnolia Electric Co.'s full-band sound, which closed out on Josephine.
Josephine closes Magnolia Electric Co.'s studio catalog, the same year Molina made a duo album with Centro-matic's Will Johnson.
Molina and Johnson makes explicit the kinship between Magnolia Electric Co. and the Denton scene, which ran parallel to What Comes After the Blues.
What Comes After the Blues extends into full-band country rock the haunted gospel sound of Didn't It Rain.
Didn't It Rain bridges Molina's solo Songs: Ohia records and the full band, following Ghost Tropic, his most slowcore album.
Ghost Tropic sounds indebted to Low- and Codeine-style slowcore, the tempo and mood Duster also borrowed.
Stratosphere filters the tempo and mood of Low and Codeine through lo-fi home recording.
I Could Live in Hope sounds indebted to Galaxie 500's pacing, and Red House Painters were stretching that same pacing longer and starker.
Down Colorful Hill's slow, confessional songs sit beside Codeine as early templates for American slowcore.
Frigid Stars stands with Galaxie 500 as an early slowcore template.
Today is tied to the Velvet Underground's hushed third album, and covers Jonathan Richman.
The Velvet Underground's quiet third album is the top of this line: slowcore's founding hush.

path: Hiss Golden Messenger to the International Submarine Band: Cosmic American Music
intro: Trunk line 7, Cosmic American Music. M.C. Taylor's Dead- and Band-indebted country soul climbs back through the 2000s revival, Emmylou and Gram, the Dead's 1970 country turn, and the first country-rock records.

steps.connection: Lateness of Dancers grows out of the homemade folk of Haw into a fuller, Dead-indebted country-rock sound.
Haw continues the path toward a full band that began with Poor Moon.
Poor Moon is a direct continuation of Bad Debt, released on the newly founded Paradise of Bachelors label.
Bad Debt's lo-fi country folk arrived as the 2000s cosmic-country revival that Beachwood Sparks helped set up was taking hold.
Beachwood Sparks is a direct descendant of Gram Parsons, whose story Emmylou Harris turned into a concept album on The Ballad of Sally Rose.
The Ballad of Sally Rose directly processes Harris's history with Gram Parsons and his last album, Grievous Angel.
Grievous Angel distills Cosmic American Music, which the Grateful Dead's 1970 country records answered from San Francisco.
American Beauty is a direct sequel to Workingman's Dead in sound and method.
Workingman's Dead grew out of the country-rock turn the Byrds and Gram Parsons made, most fully on The Gilded Palace of Sin.
The Gilded Palace of Sin carried Parsons and Chris Hillman's Byrds-honed country turn into the Flying Burrito Brothers.
Sweetheart of the Rodeo made the Byrds a country band once Parsons joined, bringing the sound he had already invented with the International Submarine Band.
Safe at Home is the top of the Cosmic American Music line: Parsons' first country-rock record, cut before Sweetheart of the Rodeo.
